title: Linking Verbs Vs Action Verbs
theory:
1 LINKING VERB + ADJECTIVE
  Linking Verbs take adjective, not adverb because they do not show action, they link the
 subject to a description (Subject complement) that describes or identifies the subject.
Linking Verb of Subject's Quality / State are therefore after Adjective comes

 gSA
  Linking Verbs: Be (is, am, are, was, were, being), look, seem, appear, feel, sound, taste,
 smell, become, get, grow, turn, remain, stay, keep, prove, etc.

 Examples Linking Verb (fn[kuk)

 1. The soup tasted delicious / deliciously.
 Look
 2. Mother looks beautiful / beautifully in the
 traditional dress.
 Action Verb (ns[kuk)

 Action Verbs take adverbs because they express action, and the adverb modifies how, when,
 where, or to what extent that action is performed.
